publish.title: Why $100 buys less every year
publish.description: Inflation shown with simple arithmetic. An illustration, not a forecast or advice.

scenes.headline: Why $100 buys less
scenes.narration: A hundred dollars today will not buy the same things in twenty years. Here is the arithmetic.

scenes.headline: Prices tend to rise
scenes.narration: Inflation is the general rise in prices over time. When prices rise, each dollar buys a little less.

scenes.headline: $100 at 3% inflation
scenes.narration: At three percent a year, a hundred dollars of buying power shrinks to about seventy-four after ten years and about fifty-five after twenty.

chart.source: Illustration: 100 divided by 1.03 to the power of the years

scenes.headline: An example, not a forecast
scenes.narration: Real inflation varies from year to year and from country to country. This is an example of the arithmetic, not a prediction.

scenes.headline: Know the number
scenes.narration: Look up your own country's inflation figure and compare it with what your savings earn. This is general education, not financial advice.
